source_snapshot.procedure: In BMC Web, add temporary static IPv4 and static DNS on all BMC ports, ping every temporary IP, then delete the test entries; source also requests log clearing.
source_snapshot.criteria: Every add and delete completes without error and each BMC static IP is reachable.
source_snapshot.script: None; 20 attended and 20 machine minutes; Test Set is mislabeled BMC Time Setting.
source_snapshot.deepseek: PARTIAL with Web/Redfish and ping, but its command only GETs interface IDs and pings the existing BMC IP, uses curl -k/password command-line patterns and does not perform or prove add/delete.
source_snapshot.gpt_v2: REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION; identity-bound per-port transactions, conflict checks, readback, independent recovery and exact baseline restoration.

historical_reviews.deepseek: The network-lockout risk is recognized, but a collection GET plus one ping cannot satisfy state mutation, all-port coverage or deletion recovery.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: Reclassification and one-port-at-a-time controls are accepted; only test-created entries may be deleted and final state must equal the captured baseline.
historical_reviews.history: Exact-code searches found no duplicate variant or completed record; the Test Set label is a category defect and does not override the aligned Network Items/Procedure/Criteria.
historical_reviews.v3_1: A static address transaction claims an identity on a management subnet and DNS configuration may affect resolution separately, so each port requires explicit mapping, ownership, reachability source and rollback evidence.

original_test_intent: With explicit approval, prove that each intended BMC port can accept an owner-approved temporary static IPv4 and DNS configuration, is reachable at that exact IP, and returns to its original network state after only the test entries are removed.
original_method: Inventory and bind every BMC Ethernet interface to a physical/logical port; preserve baseline and independent recovery; validate conflict-free per-port IPv4/DNS values; change one port at a time through the supported Web/Redfish path, read back and ping the exact temporary IP, delete only test-created data, then reconcile every field with baseline.
manual_activity: The BMC/network owner maps ports, approves temporary addresses/DNS and each mutation, observes Web behavior and maintains independent recovery while automation performs protected readback and reachability checks.
required_inputs: Complete EthernetInterface ID to physical/management-port map
Full baseline IPv4, VLAN, gateway, DHCP and DNS state per port
Conflict-free temporary static IPv4/prefix/gateway and DNS matrix
Address ownership and approved ping source/route
Supported Web or Redfish mutation/delete semantics
safety_requirements: Never write all ports from a generic instruction
Validate address ownership and conflicts before each add
Keep an independent path outside the port being changed
Use protected sessions and do not place secrets in commands/logs
Do not use curl -k without an approved bounded exception
Delete only entries created by this test
Stop on wrong port, conflict, route/DNS change, lockout or failed readback
Do not clear SEL, audit, dmesg or syslog
agent_execution_scope: Validate the approved address/DNS transaction matrix
Execute only explicitly approved supported writes one port at a time
Read back complete per-port configuration and ping the exact temporary address
engineer_actions: Approve each port, value, route, mutation and delete
Verify independent recovery and address ownership
Confirm the Web/Redfish schema and final baseline
Recover management access if needed and own PASS, FAIL or BLOCKED

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Its GET lists interface IDs and its ping targets the current BMC_IP; neither proves the required per-port add, exact temporary address, DNS write or delete.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: For each approved port, capture baseline, apply only its temporary static IPv4/DNS via the supported interface, read back all fields, ping that exact address from the approved source, delete only test entries and prove baseline restoration before the next port.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: All-port add/ping/delete scope and 20/20-minute estimates remain; unsafe simultaneous writes, TLS bypass and log clearing are prohibited.

modernized_recommendation.status: APPROVAL-GATED PER-PORT BMC IPV4 DNS TRANSACTIONS
modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Use one transaction ledger per port containing stable identity, baseline, approved temporary values, conflict check, write response, full readback, exact-address reachability, delete response and final comparison.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Replaces a blind all-port Web action and insufficient GET/ping with recoverable, identity-bound transactions and complete restoration proof.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Interface enumeration proves neither configuration nor reachability; a successful transaction on one port cannot stand for the remaining ports.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Firmware may model DNS globally rather than per interface, and writes can migrate or sever the management session; the supported schema must define ownership and atomicity.

project_override_considerations: If DNS is global, the Project must separate its lifecycle from per-port IPv4 transactions and define one authoritative baseline. Leaving test values as final state requires explicit owner approval per field rather than treating deletion as optional.
expected_evidence: Redacted SUT/BMC/interface map and complete network/DNS baseline
Approved temporary per-port values, ownership/conflict checks and independent recovery proof
Per-port protected write responses, complete readbacks and exact-IP ping outputs
Delete responses and field-by-field final equality with baseline
Management reachability, BMC audit/SEL/network events and credential/TLS audit
Engineer-owned PASS, FAIL or BLOCKED verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items, Procedure and Criteria consistently define a BMC Network add/ping/delete test. `BMC Time Setting` is a mismatched Test Set label but supplies no competing time procedure or criterion, so it is preserved as metadata rather than treated as an alternate target.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The operation is clear and becomes executable with normal owner inputs: port mapping, temporary values, supported schema, approval and independent recovery.

review_improvement: Converts an unsafe all-port mutation into per-port recoverable transactions and closes the gap between DeepSeek's GET/current-IP ping and the actual add/readback/exact-IP/delete criteria.
independent_technical_reasoning: Reachability is meaningful only for the address just assigned to the identified port, while DNS may be interface-specific or global depending on firmware. Capturing field ownership and baseline before each write is therefore required both to interpret success and to avoid deleting pre-existing management configuration.
